objective: Stewarding the PMO mandate: defining scope and authority, drafting a PMO charter, and securing executive sponsorship

sources.cite: PMI, PMI PMO Certified Professional (PMI-PMOCP) Examination Content Outline and Specifications, January 2025 (v2): Organizational Development and Alignment 16%, PMO Strategic Elements 18%, PMO Design and Structuring 18%, PMO Operation and Performance 15%, PMO Enhancement and Effectiveness 18%, People 15%

The organization, the projects and the people are fictional. The minutes or days each step takes and the effects of each decision are teaching simplifications for exam practice, not measured values.

brief.situation: You have been appointed to set up a PMO at Ashcombe Engineering, a fictional engineering firm with 60 projects across four business units. The last PMO was disbanded after a year as 'a reporting office'.
handover: The COO approved a PMO budget but has not said what it may decide.
Business unit heads expect another reporting burden.
howItWorks: The board shows the risk register against the appetite, each stakeholder's support in words and the docket.
Move on a week at a time. A decision comes to you at each review; before the first, you can read the evidence.
At the end you write the record and a short reflection.

then.log: Week 2: two business unit heads refuse to share plans; the COO is drawn into a turf dispute.
Week 3: project managers ignore the report requests; the COO asks what the PMO is for.
Week 4: a business unit overrides the PMO's resource decision; nobody senior backs the PMO.

effects.log: Week 1: what the PMO may decide.

scopePrompt.title: A PMO without defined authority
scopePrompt.context: The COO says 'just make projects better'.

choices.label: Define scope (the 60 projects above a size threshold) and decision rights: the PMO sets methods and arbitrates cross-unit resource conflicts; business units keep delivery decisions

effects.log: Scope and rights are written down.

choices.feedback: A PMO mandate states what it covers and what it may decide; without that, it becomes a reporting office.

choices.label: Make the PMO advisory only, with no decisions
choices.feedback: It can help, but cannot settle the resource conflicts the units asked for.

choices.label: Give the PMO authority over every project decision
choices.feedback: The units lose delivery decisions and resist the PMO from day one.

charterPrompt.title: What the charter says
charterPrompt.context: The COO wants a charter by month end.

choices.label: Draft a charter with purpose, services (resource arbitration, delivery support), authority, success measures and a six-month review, agreed with the business units
choices.feedback: A PMO charter records purpose, services, authority and measures, and is agreed with those it serves.

choices.label: Copy a charter template from the internet
choices.feedback: It reads well but does not reflect what the units asked for.

choices.label: Skip the charter and start collecting status reports
choices.feedback: It repeats the last PMO's mistake.

sponsorPrompt.title: A sponsor in name only
sponsorPrompt.context: The COO approved the budget and moved on.

choices.label: Ask the COO to sponsor the PMO actively: sign the charter, chair a monthly portfolio meeting and back the PMO's arbitration decisions

effects.log: The COO signs and chairs the first meeting.

choices.feedback: Executive sponsorship gives the PMO's mandate weight; without it, authority on paper is ignored.

choices.label: Ask the COO for a supportive email
Proceed without a sponsor; the budget is enough
choices.feedback: The first contested decision has nobody to back it.

reflection.question: Write the PMO charter summary for the executive team.

parts.modelAnswer: The PMO covers projects above the threshold, sets methods and arbitrates cross-unit resource conflicts; units keep delivery decisions. The charter is agreed.

parts.label: Sponsorship
parts.criteria: The COO signs, chairs and backs decisions.
parts.modelAnswer: The COO signed the charter, chairs the monthly portfolio meeting and backs arbitration decisions.

scoring.modelReasoning: A PMO's mandate defines its scope and decision rights, written into a charter agreed with the units it serves, and backed by an active executive sponsor. Without them, a PMO becomes a reporting office.
